title: Costa Rica bars UN special rapporteur on Palestinian territories from entering country over ‘links to terrorist acts’ | CNN
text:
Source: CNN

Costa Rica has denied entry to a United Nations special rapporteur focused on thehuman rights of Palestinians,citing national security concerns after she was subject to an “international alert over links to terrorist acts.”

Francesca Albanese, an independent expert appointed by the UN to follow and report on human rights in the Palestinian territories, was held for more than a day at Juan Santamaría International Airport, near the capital San José. Early Saturday, she said she was outside the airport, after earlier saying the country’s constitutional court had ruled that she could be taken to a hotel.

The Italian lawyer had traveled to the Central American country to receive an honorary doctorate from the University of Costa Rica.

Omer Badilla, director general of Costa Rica’s immigration authority, said in a video statement on Thursday that authorities had denied Albanese entry because she was the subject of an “international alert over links to terrorist acts.”

He did not specify the source of the alert or provide evidence to substantiate the allegation. “When national security is compromised, as it is in this case, our police authorities strictly enforce the provisions of our legal system,” he said.

“Defending human rights is not terrorism,” Albanese said in anX poston Friday.

Hours before she was allowed to leave the airport Saturday, she said she had already been awake for 50 hours, adding that she had a flight scheduled on Saturday.

She was appointed in 2022 to her role and has become an outspoken critic of Israel’s military actions in Gaza,accusing the countryof committing genocide against Palestinians. Last year, she was accused of working with the International Criminal Court (ICC) to pursue legal action against US and Israeli nationals and was sanctioned by the United States.

In an interviewwith Costa Rican newspaper La Nación Friday, Albanese pushed back against the accusation from Costa Rican authorities. “If you have evidence, you will have to present it, if you don’t, you will have to answer for your words,” she said.

CNN has reached out to Costa Rica’s presidency, Ministry of Foreign Affairs for comment.

UN High Commissioner for Human Rights Volker Türk said Friday he was “deeply concerned” by the decision to deny Albanese entry on claimed national security grounds.

“This is difficult to reconcile with Costa Rica’s longstanding commitment to human rights,” Türk said, urging authorities to reconsider their decision and allow Albanese into the country.

The Italian Foreign Ministry said that Albanese remained in the international area of the airport and had not formally entered Costa Rican territory.

The University of Costa Rica went ahead with its ceremony Friday, which saw Albanese participate remotely from the airport.

The universitypreviouslycalled on immigration authorities and the country’s foreign ministry to explain the legal grounds for their decision. “A UN rapporteur being unable to enter the country to receive an academic distinction is a matter of enormous gravity,” the university said.

In her acceptance speech, Albanese rejected the Costa Rican government’s allegations and called for an investigation into whether her denial of entry was connected to sanctions imposed on her by the US Treasury Department.

CNN has reached out to the US State Department for comment.

Albanese said she had chosen to remain at the airport to participate in the ceremony, thanking Costa Rican citizens, activists and academics for their support.

She also said sanctions had prevented her from traveling to the United States last month to present her latest report to the UN General Assembly, forcing her to participate remotely as well.

Israel’s UN envoy Danny Danon praised Costa Rica’s decision on X, accusing Albanese of using her UN mandate to spread propaganda against Israel and the US.

Costa Rica’s government, led by right-wing President Laura Fernández, has maintained close ties with the Trump administration, cooperating with the US on security and immigration. In September, Fernández said US military operations on Costa Rican soil could benefit the country’s national security.

When the Trump administration announced sanctions on Albanese in July 2025, US Secretary of State Marco Rubio accused her of antisemitism and expressing support for terrorism – allegations she has rejected.

The sanctions came shortly after Albanese published a report accusing several American companies of profiting “from the Israeli economy of illegal occupation, apartheid and now genocide.”

The US had also opposed the renewal of Albanese’s mandate and called for her removal as special rapporteur.

On Thursday night, from the airport, she wrote on X: “You know the face of the empire the day you get on its nerves or cross its boundaries.”

CNN’s Stefano Pozzebon and Anabella Gonzalez contributed reporting.

CNN’s Stefano Pozzebon and Anabella Gonzalez contributed reporting.
